_arch_note: PARALLEL ADDITIVE FFN+LUT, NO GATE (task f1c19715). All 6 layers identical: h=ln2(x), then o = FFN(h) + LUT(h) (plain SUM, no convex gate, no LayerScale, no forced mixing), residual x_out = x + o. Distinct from 0217 (convex gate) and 0218 (series residual-stack). Branch A dense FFN NARROWED: 2-layer GELU MLP with dense_inner_dim=384 (=d_model, no 4x), same as 0219. Branch B LUT REDUCED: CompressionMHL light/constant/margin, read_top_n=1, H=4 tph=128 (n_tables=512), nap=8 (256 cells), inner_in=inner_out=48 -> H*inner_in=4*48=192, so compress is 384->192 (genuine input rank reduction) and decompress 192->384. Both branch output projections zeroed at init (mlp last Linear + LUT decompress weight) so the block is identity at init and BOTH branches train up from zero. This is the 'narrowed-FFN + small-LUT deficit-recovery' test: does adding a cheap reduced-rank LUT in parallel recover the loss a narrowed (1x) FFN gives up vs the full 4x FFN? Same 16k schedule as 0135/0176/0219/0220 (n_steps=16000, warmup 1600, cosine to 0.1x floor, peak 3e-4, wd 0.1, d_model=384 6L 6h seq512, untied, seed 1, corrected fixed eval), device_batch 12 x ga4 = 24576. TRITON_CACHE_DIR set. Queued behind 0219/0220 if GPU tight.
